titleEn: Big Light On, Little Light Off!

pages.text: "Not bedtime! More shells to stack!" Dari piled shells on the bedroom floor. The sea darkened beyond the round window. Holding back a yawn, he called, "A little longer!"
Dad, the lighthouse keeper, peeked in. "I'm going up to turn on the big light. Come help? Then it's bedtime." "I'm not sleepy!" Dari shook his head and hugged his shell tower.
But his eyes kept closing. Shells slipped from his front flippers. A huge yawn escaped. "Am I a little sleepy?"
Mom carried Dari up the spiral stairs to the top room. Windows surrounded a huge lighthouse lamp. Dad held its brass handle. "Together, Dari."
Dad and Dari laid their flippers together and turned. Click—light! A bright beam stretched far across the dark sea. "Wow!" Dari's head and tail both rose.

Through the windows, the island was visible. Faraway mainland lights went out one by one. Boats rocked to sleep at the dock. Dad whispered, "Big light on, and everyone turns little lights off to sleep."
They went down to the bedroom. Dari slipped under his quilt. Mom kissed his forehead and sang, "Big light on, little light off!" She blew out the little bedroom lamp.
The lighthouse beam swept past the round window, around and around. Dari looked at his tower. "Sleep tight, shells." He tapped his tail flippers beneath the quilt and closed his eyes.
Now Dari knew bedtime's steps. "One, big light on—stop playing! Two, under the quilt! Three, little light off and sleep!" Only soft breathing filled the room.
Morning! The lighthouse lamp was off, and the round window bright. Mom cuddled Dari. "A good sleep makes morning sparkle!" Big light on, little light off! Now Dari liked bedtime.
